name: Server-side prototype pollution
description:
The application merges a posted JSON body into server-side objects without dropping the __proto__ key, so a client can write properties onto the server-side object prototype that every object inherits. The finding was proven non-destructively: a {"__proto__":{"json spaces":10}} member changed how the endpoint serialised its own JSON responses (or a {"__proto__":{"status":510}} member changed the status of its error answers), and a null member reverted the change. Both are documented detection techniques for the class; the same write primitive can, with the right property, alter authorisation decisions, option lookups, or template resolution server-side.

This row is burpsy's own: Burp's catalogue covers only the client-side (DOM) form, and Burp tests the server-side class by hand or with a BApp under the generic extension-generated type.
remediation: Merge user-supplied JSON with a routine that drops __proto__, constructor and prototype keys, or build target objects with Object.create(null) semantics. Validate request bodies against a schema that rejects unknown top-level members. Where the runtime allows, freeze Object.prototype on services that merge untrusted JSON.
